sources.entry: AWS Graviton Getting Started - Where AWS states which Neoverse core, ISA revision, mesh, caches and compiler flag each Graviton generation carries.

summary.one_liner: A technical guide from AWS covering how to build, tune, and migrate software to Amazon EC2 instances powered by Graviton processors (Graviton2 through Graviton5).
summary.what_it_does: The README is a large index of guidance for running code on Arm-based AWS Graviton EC2 instances. Its core content is a comparison table across Graviton2, 3/3E, 4, and 5 listing the Neoverse core, frequency, interconnect, Armv8/Armv9 revision, supported instruction features, recommended -mcpu compiler flag, core counts, and L1/L2/LLC cache sizes. The table section is the part that answers the query about per-generation core, ISA revision, mesh, caches, and compiler flag. The rest of the contents list covers transitioning workloads, language-specific notes (C/C++, Go, Java, Python, Rust, Node.js, and others), containers, Lambda, Linux kernel, OS support, machine learning frameworks (PyTorch, llama.cpp, TensorFlow, vLLM, ONNX), HPC, Spark, and known issues. The README also points to Agent Skills for assisting x86-to-Graviton migrations of Java, Python, and .NET code, and includes curated blog posts and case studies. The excerpt provided is truncated partway through the table and the later sections, so only the visible portion was used.
use_cases: compare Graviton generations by core and ISA
choose a compiler -mcpu flag for Graviton
migrate x86 workloads to Arm64 EC2
tune Java, Python, or C++ code for Graviton
run ML inference like PyTorch or llama.cpp on Arm CPUs
plan a transition of workloads to Graviton
notable: Side-by-side Graviton2 to Graviton5 table of Neoverse core, Armv revision, CMN interconnect, and cache sizes
Lists recommended -mcpu compiler flag per generation (for example neoverse-512tvb for Graviton3 onward)
Agent Skills for AI-assisted x86-to-Graviton migrations of Java, Python, and .NET projects
Broad per-language and per-framework guidance including ML, HPC, Spark, and containers
caveats: The provided README excerpt is truncated; later sections are not visible and were not summarized in detail
Content is specific to AWS Graviton EC2 instances and does not apply to other cloud or x86 hardware
Blog and case study links may become outdated as Graviton generations change
